summary: K/JS: rootPackageJson fails with NLP when testPackageJson skipped and main packageJson up-to-date
description:
There is case, which now provokes `rootPackageJson` to fail with NLP.

1. No `binaries.executable()`
2. Run `assemble` (only main `packageJson` tasks executed without execution of `rootPackageJson` and `kotlinNpmInstall`)
3. Run `check` (it provokes to execute `testPackageJson` and `rootPackageJson` ). All `packageJson` tasks are already up-to-date. But one module which other modules do not depend on can skip `testPackageJson`, so this means main `packageJson` task of this module has no "resolution" in our infrastructure, and NLP happens.

summary: K/JS, K/Wasm: kotlinNpmInstall can rewrite root package.json
description:
Now `kotlinNpmInstall` uses our state-machine mechanism of resolving dependencies to correct work with our project's `package.json` and root `package.json`.

But looking on how `kotlinNpmInstall` works now, it does not require result of dependency resolution.

Case:

* Change `version` in root `package.json` after its generation - in `doLast` block
* Run build
* Root `package.json` contains correct `version`
* Remove `node_modules`
* Run build
* `rootPackageJson` is up-to-date (so version is not rewritten)
* But `kotlinNpmInstall` regenerate root `package.json` and change its version to incorrect

description:
If I have two included gradle builds, and included build 1 depends on an artifact provided by included build 2, Kotlin/JS compilation fails.

A minimal reproducer is [attached](multiple-siblings.zip). Run `:reproduce` from `parent`. It models this tree:
```
root folder
\ - parent
\ - child1
\ - child2
```

The project is built from `parent`, and both `child1` and `child2` are included from it. `child1` does not explicitly include `child2`. However, if `child1` depends (potentially transitively) on an artifact provided by `child2`, this artifact will still be substituted. At this point, Kotlin/JS explodes.

This setup is common when compositing local snapshot builds of dependencies; we ran into this when working on [Signum](https://github.com/a-sit-plus/signum), which composites in local clones of [awesn1](https://github.com/a-sit-plus/awesn1) and [Multibase](https://github.com/a-sit-plus/multibase) this way.

I suspect the issue is in `KotlinCompilationNpmResolver::visitCompositeProjectDependency`, which [assumes](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/blob/v2.4.10/libraries/tools/kotlin-gradle-plugin/src/common/kotlin/org/jetbrains/kotlin/gradle/targets/js/npm/resolver/KotlinCompilationNpmResolver.kt#L303) that the substituted build is included _by the current project_. This does not have to be the case.

KT-47351 is potentially related.

summary: Replace KotlinPackageJsonTask as the source of shared npm project package.json files
description: In KT-89214, two new consumable configurations were introduced, `kotlinNpmSharedPackageJsonFiles` and `kotlinWasmNpmSharedPackageJsonFiles`, to which each registered subproject adds its `package.json` collected from `compilation.npmProject.packageJsonFile`, the output of `KotlinPackageJsonTask`. That task depends on the root-project npm resolver: tooling `devDependencies` (karma, mocha, webpack, playwright) only appear when the root `rootPackageJson` task is configured, so `kotlinSetupSharedNpmProject` alone produces test `package.json` files without them, and transitive dependencies are collected by reading other projects' models, which is not Isolated Projects compatible. Implement an alternative approach to collect the npm dependencies of subprojects.

Take this piece of code:

```kotlin
@Suppress("NO_ACTUAL_CLASS_MEMBER_FOR_EXPECTED_CLASS")
public actual typealias ZByteArray = ByteArray

@Suppress("NOTHING_TO_INLINE")
public actual inline operator fun ZByteArray.set(index: Int, value: Byte): Unit =
  throw UnsupportedOperationException("This should never be called at runtime")
```

Over `ZByteArray.set` you'll see an `EXTENSION_SHADOWED_BY_MEMBER` warning:

![](image.png)

Being the warning says *shadowed* I'd expect it to never be called at runtime, and **it was like that in 1.9.24**.
With 2.0.20-Beta2, I have failing tests because the extension function is called:

```

	at com.hcl.mainframe.proto.hex.HexConverterImpl.convertToChars(HexConverterImpl.kt:49)
```

What is the expected behavior here?
